cover.headline: India's best hotel franchise, priced as if the 2026 hotel-stock sell-off never happened
cover.lead: IHCL owns or runs 382 hotels (33,609 keys) under Taj, Vivanta, Gateway, SeleQtions and Ginger, plus 51% of airline caterer TajSATS, and has another ~32,600 keys signed, 81% of them managed for a fee. Q1FY27 revenue rose 15% and management fees 26%; the company guides 12-14% growth for FY27. The street values IHCL on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E (23-30x)** and is almost all Buy (post-Q1 targets average ₹853). We forecast EBITDA of ₹3,673 / 4,169 / 4,655 cr and EPS of ₹15.0 / 17.3 / 19.5 (FY27-29E), close to the street. The difference is the multiple. Listed hotel peers had de-rated ~33% against their own medians by 30-Sep-2026 (EIH −26%, Lemon Tree −39%); IHCL had not (it sat at 26.2x one-year-forward EV/EBITDA, at its post-Covid median of 26.0x). Applying the house rule gives **17.5x Sep-28E EBITDA** and a sum of the parts of **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with SELL.** Cross-checks agree: P/E ₹478, DCF ₹418. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A real moat at the top end
arguments.p: Taj is India's strongest brand five years running (Brand Finance); IHCL owns irreplaceable city and palace hotels and is the largest operator in the country. Standalone occupancy was 82% in Q1FY27 and hotel operating margins ~34% for FY26. Management fees (₹685 cr in FY26, +22%) are ~8.4% of hotel revenue and almost all profit.

arguments.h: Growth is good but partly bought
arguments.p: Of the 12-14% FY27 guide, 4-5 points come from new hotels and acquisitions (ANK/Pride, Atmantan, Brij, ₹250 cr+ of revenue); like-for-like growth is 7-9%, mostly rate. TajSATS (51%) grew 3% in Q1 and earns ~20-24% margins. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}} / +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} and EPS growth of ~14% a year (FY26-29E, before one-offs).

arguments.h: Rich balance sheet, shrinking share of the profit
arguments.p: Net cash ~₹4,300 cr before leases (AAA). But minorities took ~7% of profit in FY26 and ~8% in Q1FY27 (TajSATS 49%, PIEM, Benares, and 49% of every 2025-26 acquisition), and exceptional items appear every year. ROCE is 17.4% against a 20%+ target.

arguments.h: Valuation: the sector re-priced, IHCL did not
arguments.p: At ₹729 the market pays ~24.3x Sep-28E hotel EBITDA once the other parts are valued our way; our derived multiple is 17.5x. The DCF says the same thing from another angle: today's price needs a ~9.6% discount rate against our 12.2% cost of equity. We would buy below ~₹470.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): management expected Q2 growth to match or beat Q1's 14.6%; watch like-for-like RevPAR, the TajSATS recovery and the Frankfurt ramp-up.
The West Asia conflict and airline capacity: inbound, MICE and international hotels (Dubai, London, The Pierre) and TajSATS volumes.
The Oriental Hotels merger (25 IHCL shares for 117 OHL shares; ~2.32 cr new shares, ~1.6% dilution): approvals through FY27, completion targeted in H2FY28.
Peak season (Oct-Mar): weddings (40+ auspicious dates in the rest of FY27), BRICS 2026, Aero India and Vibrant Gujarat events.
Further deals: management says M&A is "an ongoing exercise"; each 51% deal adds revenue but also minorities.

sections.title: India's largest hotel company: owner of the trophy hotels, manager of most of the rest, and 51% of the biggest airline caterer

blocks.p: IHCL earns money three ways. **It owns or leases hotels** (134 hotels, 13,355 keys at Jun-2026: the Taj Mahal Palace in Mumbai, Taj Palace and Taj Mahal in Delhi, Rambagh and Lake Palace in Rajasthan, Fort Aguada in Goa, plus The Pierre in New York, St James Court in London and, since Jun-2026, the leased Taj Hessischer Hof in Frankfurt) and keeps all their revenue and costs. **It manages hotels owned by others** (228 hotels, 18,531 keys) for a fee, typically a share of revenue plus a share of profit; fees were ₹685 cr in FY26. **It runs adjacent businesses**: Ginger (midscale, ~166 hotels), Qmin (food), ama (homestays), Tree of Life, Atmantan (wellness, 51% since Jan-2026), Brij (boutique, 51% since Apr-2026) and TajSATS (airline catering, 51%, consolidated since Aug-2024).

**Brands by price point:** Taj (luxury, 93 operating hotels), Claridges Collection, Vivanta and SeleQtions (upscale), Gateway (upscale relaunch), Ginger (midscale and economy, the largest by hotel count) and Tree of Life (boutique leisure). In FY26 the consolidated hotel segment earned ₹8,487 cr: rooms 50%, food and beverage 33%, other operating income 8% and management fees 8%. About 80% of consolidated hotel revenue is domestic; the international portfolio (New York, London, Cape Town, Dubai and Maldives management contracts) earned ₹1,725 cr of revenue and ₹250 cr of EBITDA in FY26.

blocks.callout: **Why the mix matters for investors:** the owned hotels are where the value and the capital sit (they make most of the EBITDA and need ₹1,000-1,300 cr of capex a year); the managed hotels and brands are where the growth sits (81% of the pipeline) and they need almost no capital. Air catering is a different, lower-margin business that came with the 2024 TajSATS consolidation. A single group multiple blurs all three; the street and we value them inside one EV/EBITDA, with TajSATS and minorities treated separately.

sections.title: Demand ahead of supply for a fourth year, but growth is slowing and the 2026 travel shock hit the sector's valuation

blocks.p: Branded hotel rooms in India are scarce relative to demand: in key cities branded supply grows ~5% a year (FY25-27; Delhi ~5%, Mumbai 5%, Bengaluru 6%, Goa nil), while ICRA expected premium-hotel demand to grow 8-10% a year over FY25-28 against 5-6% supply. That gap has let hotels push room rates up for four years. But growth is slowing from the post-Covid rebound: ICRA (29-Sep-2026) expects premium-hotel revenue to grow 7-9% in FY27 after 11% in FY26, with occupancy of 72-74% and average room rates of Rs8,600-8,800. The 2026 West Asia conflict cut flights and lifted fuel costs, hitting inbound travel, long-haul corridors and airline catering; domestic leisure and weddings held up (HVS Anarock: June-2026 RevPAR +17-19% on a weak base; Q2 CY26 +11-13%).

blocks.title: Tailwind test

sections.title: Hotels: rate-led growth at high occupancy; 2026 shows how fast travel shocks hit the international hotels

blocks.p: The hotel segment (88% of revenue, 91% of operating EBITDA in FY26) grew 11% in FY26 and 17% in Q1FY27. Occupancy in like-for-like consolidated hotels was 76% in both FY25 and FY26, so growth came from price: like-for-like RevPAR (revenue per available room) rose 9% to ₹11,750. Standalone hotels (the Indian owned portfolio) did better in Q1FY27: occupancy 82% (76% a year earlier), operating margin 38.7% (+4 pp), helped by renovated rooms at Taj Palace Delhi, The President Mumbai, Taj West End and Fort Aguada and the new Varanasi wing (PBT-positive in its first quarter). The weak spots are abroad: St James Court's EBITDA fell from ₹48 cr to ₹36 cr in Q1 (renovation, West Asia), and The Pierre (UOH) earns a 7.7% margin.

blocks.callout: **So what:** the domestic owned hotels are an excellent business (standalone operating margin 42% in FY26) and their rate power is visible in every quarter. Growth from here is a mix of 7-9% like-for-like rate gains and new keys. We assume room revenue grows 15% / 11% / 10% (FY27-29E) and hotel margins edge up from 34.3% to 36.0%.

sections.title: Management fees and the growth brands: the best part of the story, still under a tenth of hotel revenue

blocks.p: Management fees grew from ₹399 cr (FY23) to ₹685 cr (FY26), 20% a year, and 26% in Q1FY27 (₹168 cr) despite weaker Dubai, Sri Lanka and Maldives hotels. Management guides "high-teens" growth on a pipeline of ~26,250 managed keys, about 1.4x today's managed inventory. Fees carry almost no cost, so they lift margins and returns: we estimate fees at 8.4% of hotel revenue in FY27E rising to 9.5% in FY29E (₹815 cr → ₹1,125 cr). The "new businesses" (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life) reached ₹753 cr of revenue in FY26 (+25%); Ginger alone ₹709 cr at a 44% EBITDAR margin (Ginger Mumbai Airport ₹105 cr at 56%), and ₹183 cr in Q1FY27 (+20%).

sections.title: TajSATS: a solid market leader in airline catering, but a lower-margin business that came in with the 2024 consolidation

blocks.p: TajSATS (IHCL 51%, SATS of Singapore 49%) is India's largest airline caterer: management says it supplies over half of all meals served in the air. It became a subsidiary on 1-Aug-2024 after the shareholders' agreement was amended (IHCL booked a ₹307 cr fair-value gain). FY26 operating revenue was ₹1,210 cr with a 23.7% operating margin (a new airport levy passed through revenue costs ~1-2 pp of margin); Q1FY27 revenue rose only 3% to ₹296 cr and the margin fell to 19.5% as West Asia flight cuts hit international meals and the new Noida (Jewar) kitchen started up. Management expects growth to return to double digits within "three to six months" and then 15-20%. FY26 profit was ₹173 cr, of which ₹85 cr belonged to SATS.

Pricing power in luxury; helps sign management contracts.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** IHCL has a genuine moat in luxury and upper-upscale India, where the brand and the buildings earn premium rates and win management contracts. That moat is worth a premium multiple over other Indian hotel companies, and the market gives it one. It does not protect earnings from travel shocks (Covid, 2026 West Asia), and it does not extend to Ginger or air catering.

sections.title: Revenue more than doubled from pre-Covid and margins rose by 11 points; profit before one-offs grew ~25% a year since FY23

blocks.p: Consolidated revenue was ₹4,463 cr in FY20, collapsed to ₹1,575 cr in FY21 (Covid) and reached ₹9,689 cr in FY26: 19% a year over FY23-26. Part of the recent growth is bought or consolidated: TajSATS became a subsidiary in Aug-2024 (₹717 cr of revenue in FY25, ₹1,210 cr in FY26), ANK/Pride joined in Dec-2025, Atmantan in Jan-2026 and Brij in Apr-2026. The hotel business alone grew from ₹6,769 cr (FY24) to ₹8,487 cr (FY26), 12% a year. Operating EBITDA margin moved from 22% (FY20) to 31% (FY23) and 33% (FY26) as room rates rose faster than costs and management fees (almost all profit) grew. Profit attributable to owners before exceptional items went from ₹956 cr (FY23) to ₹1,849 cr (FY26); reported profit is higher (₹2,084 cr) because of a ₹399 cr gain on selling the Taj GVK stake.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is the best-run large hotel company in India, and the post-Covid profit recovery is real: margins are 11 points above FY20 and the balance sheet went from net debt to ~₹4,300 cr of net cash. But three things flatter the headline growth: consolidation of TajSATS, acquisitions, and exceptional gains in each of the last two years. On a like-for-like basis the hotels grow at high single digits to low double digits.

sections.title: Cash generation funds renovations, acquisitions and rising dividends; returns are up but still well below the 20% target

blocks.p: IHCL turns ~78% of operating EBITDA into operating cash (FY26: ₹2,471 cr of ₹3,196 cr). Capex was ₹637 cr in FY24 and ~₹1,050 cr a year in FY25-26 (₹2,500 cr+ over three years: Taj Mahal Palace, Taj Palace Delhi, The President, Fort Aguada, Varanasi expansion, Ekta Nagar), and the company guides ₹1,100-1,300 cr for FY27. Acquisitions took ~₹420 cr in FY26 (ANK/Pride ₹190 cr, Atmantan ₹232 cr) and ~₹222 cr in Apr-2026 (Brij), partly funded by the ₹592 cr Taj GVK sale. Dividends rose from ₹155 cr (FY24) to ₹342 cr (FY26). The company's pre-tax ROCE was 13% in FY23 and 17.4% in FY26; the Accelerate 2030 target is 20%+, which needs more managed hotels and fewer rupees per key on the balance sheet.

blocks.callout: **The capital question:** IHCL can fund ₹1,100-1,300 cr of capex, ₹400-500 cr of dividends and bolt-on deals from cash flow and still add to its ₹4,400 cr cash pile. The risk is not the balance sheet but returns: owned luxury keys cost ₹2-4 cr each to build and renovations are now a permanent ~₹650 cr a year. Every new owned project (Bandstand ~450 keys, Shiroda, Lakshadweep) dilutes ROCE for years before it adds to it.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audits and strong cash, but exceptional items every year and a rising minority share

bullets: **Exceptional items.** Exceptional items in each of the last five years (FY22 +48, FY23 +64, FY24 +24, FY25 +345, FY26 +309 on Screener; company FY26 net +236 after tax). FY25-26 gains are one-off (TajSATS fair-value, Taj GVK sale) but recurring smaller charges (key money, labour codes, contingencies) also sit below the line. FY26 reported PAT ₹2,084 cr vs ₹1,849 cr before exceptional items; FY25 ₹1,908 cr vs ₹1,603 cr. We value and forecast on profit before exceptional items.

**Minorities.** Partners own 49% of TajSATS, 41% of PIEM, 48% of Benares, 20% of St James Court and 49% of ANK, Pride, Atmantan and Brij. FY26: TajSATS ₹85 cr, PIEM ₹40 cr, Benares ₹21 cr, St James Court ₹7 cr, others ₹11 cr = ~₹163 cr (7% of profit before minorities, up from 5% in FY23-24); ₹33 cr in Q1FY27 alone. Every 2025-26 deal adds a 49% partner. Minority interest on the balance sheet rose from ₹672 cr to ₹1,887 cr in two years.

**Leases.** Ind AS 116: lease liabilities Rs2,786 cr (Mar-26), right-of-use assets Rs2,287 cr; rent is below EBITDA (interest + depreciation), so EBITDA flatters leased hotels versus owned ones. License fees (revenue-share leases) stay in opex (Rs385 cr in FY26 hotel segment).
**Goodwill.** Goodwill rose to Rs1,121 cr (Mar-26) from Rs711 cr after ANK/Pride and Atmantan.
**TajSATS revenue.** TajSATS revenue now includes an airport levy passed through, which lowers its reported margin (~1-2.3 pp).
**Cash conversion.** Operating cash 77% of EBITDA in FY26 (79% in FY25); company free cash flow ₹1,450 cr = 75% of profit before exceptional items.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing aggressive in the accounts, and the cash is real (net cash ~₹4,300 cr, AAA rating). But reported profit has been lifted by one-off gains in each of the last two years, smaller charges keep appearing below the line (key money, labour codes, contingencies), and the share of profit going to minority partners is rising with each 51% acquisition.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹4,300 cr before leases; ~₹1,500 cr after leases; minorities are now ₹1,887 cr of the balance sheet

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 IHCL had ₹4,345 cr of cash and liquid investments and only ₹51 cr of bank debt: **net cash of ₹4,294 cr** on the company's measure (₹4,439 cr gross at Jun-2026). Lease liabilities of ₹2,786 cr (hotels run on long leases, e.g. The Pierre in New York, St James Court in London, Frankfurt from Jun-2026) are debt-like, so **net cash after leases was ~₹1,510 cr**. Screener counts ₹1,107 cr of strategic investments (JVs and associates at ₹567 cr of book value, plus equity stakes) as investments too, which takes its net cash measure, and our model's, to ₹2,600 cr. Two other items matter for valuation: minorities rose from ₹672 cr (Mar-24) to ₹1,887 cr (Mar-26) as TajSATS and the 51% acquisitions came in, and goodwill rose to ₹1,121 cr. ICRA upgraded IHCL to AAA (Stable) in FY26.

sections.title: Our forecasts: revenue ~11-14% a year, EBITDA ~13%, EPS ~14% before one-offs; close to the street

blocks.p: We forecast the hotel segment stream by stream (rooms, F&B, other operating income, management fees; the authoring script checks that the build equals model hotel revenue), air catering on its own growth and margin, and a small inter-segment elimination. Group EBITDA is the sum of the segments (operating, post-Ind AS 116), so lease liabilities count as debt and new leases sit in capex. Other income is built from treasury yield on gross cash plus dividends. Depreciation is 3.8% of gross block; tax plus minorities less associates 31% of profit before tax (the engine has no minority line); payout 20%. Every assumption and our reasoning is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet, which recalculates the target.

sections.title: The street: ten of thirteen Buy, targets ₹676-925, all on EV/EBITDA FY28E at 23-30x

blocks.p: After the Q1FY27 results (21-Jul-2026) the houses that published raised or kept their targets: ICICI Securities ₹925 (SOTP, 30x Jun-28E EV/EBITDA, kept on 27-Aug), Jefferies ₹875 (reiterated 17-Sep), Motilal Oswal ₹870 (SOTP, 28x FY28E), ICICI Direct ₹865 (29x FY28E), Anand Rathi ₹845 (~26x), Macquarie ₹840, Axis ₹830 (27x), Nomura ₹830 (~23x); Morgan Stanley stays Equal-weight (₹783). Post-Q1 targets average ~₹853; the median of all thirteen standing notes is ₹840. Earlier and more cautious: Nuvama Hold ₹676 and Elara Accumulate ₹716 (both 12-May-2026, after the West Asia shock). Bulls argue the hotel upcycle has years to run (supply ~5% a year vs demand 8-10%), IHCL will beat its 12-14% guide, and fees and Ginger make the model lighter every year. No note we found adjusted the multiple for the sector's 2026 de-rating.

blocks.p: Every house that discloses a method uses **EV/EBITDA** (enterprise value ÷ operating profit) on FY28E or Jun-28E EBITDA. Three (Motilal Oswal, ICICI Securities, Anand Rathi) turn it into a sum of the parts: hotels on EV/EBITDA, TajSATS at IHCL's 51%, Oriental Hotels at market value, less minorities, plus net cash. blocks.p: House rule: start from the stock's own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA, adjust for how far the sector had moved against its own history by 30-Sep-2026, then test growth, peers, returns and the street. Two choices follow the settled rules. (1) **Window.** IHCL's EBITDA broke from a Covid loss (FY21 −₹362 cr, FY22 ₹405 cr) to ₹1,805 cr in FY23; on realised forward EBITDA the 2021-22 multiples look artificially low (13-18x) because the market could not see the rebound. The turnaround rule starts the window at the break (1-Apr-2022) and measures the peers' move over the same window; the since-2021 median is a sensitivity row. (2) **EV includes minorities.** Because the SOTP values 100% of hotel EBITDA and then deducts minorities, the history grosses market value up by each year's minority share of profit (5-7%); without it the median is 24.2x.

sections.title: Our honest summary: buy the franchise, not at this price

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's strongest hotel brand and its best trophy assets, ~82% occupancy in the owned Indian hotels, a fee stream compounding at ~20%, a fast-growing midscale arm, ~₹4,400 cr of cash and a Tata parent. Earnings should grow ~13-15% a year.

**What you are paying:** 26.2x one-year-forward EV/EBITDA (its own post-Covid median is 26.0x) and 42.2x our FY28E EPS, while listed hotel peers trade ~33% below their own medians. On the street's method with our inputs and the house rule for the multiple, the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a SELL. The rating rests on the sector adjustment; without it the same SOTP gives roughly ₹790 (a HOLD).

What it means

Hotels IHCL owns or rents; it books all their revenue and costs. Revenue-share ("capital-light") leases: the owner pays for the building and IHCL pays a share of revenue.

Accounting rule that puts leases on the balance sheet: rent becomes depreciation and interest, and future rent a lease liability.

assumptions._unallocLabel: Corporate costs not in any segment
assumptions._unallocWhy: Segments sum to consolidated operating EBITDA as reported (FY26 Rs2,907 + Rs287 = Rs3,194 cr vs Rs3,195 cr; Screener Rs3,196 cr).

businessLines._why: Hotel segment build (Rs cr). FY26 base: room 4,283, F&B 2,829, other operating income 690, management fees 685 = 8,487 (Q4FY26 deck slide 45). Growth per stream in segments[0]._why.

assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex guide Rs1,100-1,300 cr for FY27 and Rs1,000-1,200 cr a year after (renovations, greenfield on-balance-sheet keys: Bandstand, Shiroda, Lakshadweep, Ginger Goa Mopa, Bengaluru airport) plus ~Rs100-150 cr a year of new leases (right-of-use; Frankfurt in FY27), because the model's net cash deducts lease liabilities. FY26 capex Rs1,037 cr, FY25 Rs1,074 cr. Brij (Rs222 cr, Apr-2026) is not in capex; it is in the net cash bridge in the valuation chapter.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs605 cr = 3.8% of average gross block (Rs15,911 cr incl. right-of-use); Q1FY27 Rs163 cr (Rs652 cr annualised). 3.8% gives FY27E ~Rs670 cr with Frankfurt.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Zero: the engine would apply it to net cash after lease liabilities. Treasury income is built on gross cash in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from AR FY26 consolidated note 25 (Rs282 cr): treasury Rs219 cr (bank interest Rs93 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs126 cr) on ~Rs3,700 cr average gross cash = ~5.9%; dividends on equity investments Rs33 cr; other Rs30 cr. FY27E: ~6% on ~Rs4,700 cr average gross cash (Rs4,439 cr at Jun-26) = ~Rs280 cr + dividends ~Rs35 cr + other ~Rs15 cr = Rs330 cr (Q1FY27 Rs80 cr x 4 = Rs320 cr). Then +Rs30 cr a year as cash builds. Excludes exceptional items (Screener's FY26 Rs557 cr includes Rs309 cr of them) and the share of associates (in the tax rate).
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs221 cr with gross bank debt of only Rs51 cr: it is almost all interest on Rs2,786 cr of lease liabilities. Q1FY27 Rs57 cr (Rs228 cr annualised); Frankfurt lease from Jun-2026 adds ~Rs10 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities less associates (engine workaround: no minority or associate line). FY26 before exceptional items: PBT Rs2,650 cr, PAT before minorities and associates Rs1,960 cr (tax 26.0%), associates + minorities -Rs111 cr, attributable PAT Rs1,849 cr = 30.2% leakage. Q1FY27: PBT Rs533 cr to Rs358 cr = 32.8% (associates nil). 31%: tax ~25.5% + minorities ~6.5% of PBT (TajSATS 49%, PIEM 41%, Benares 48%, St James 20%, ANK/Pride/Atmantan/Brij 49%) less associates ~1%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: FY26 dividend Rs3.25 a share (incl. a special Rs0.50) = 22% of reported EPS; Rs2.75 ordinary = 21% of EPS before exceptional items. 20%.

dcf._betaWhy: Net cash after lease liabilities, so the 12.2% cost of equity is also the WACC; beta 0.95: travel demand is cyclical (Covid, West Asia) but IHCL has no financial leverage.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian travel and hotel spending grows with nominal GDP; 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10-11% to 8% by year 15 as like-for-like rate growth normalises and the managed pipeline matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 34%: hotel margins ~36% diluted by TajSATS (~23%) and leased hotels; FY26 33.0%.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex fades from ~11% of revenue to 8% (renovation ~5% plus growth keys); FY26 10.7%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: West Asia normalises by H2FY27, like-for-like RevPAR grows ~10% a year (Jefferies case), Frankfurt and the acquisitions ramp fast, fees compound at 20%+ and the market pays the top quartile of IHCL's own post-Covid multiple range after the same sector move.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The 2026 travel shock lingers: inbound and MICE stay weak, like-for-like RevPAR grows ~4-5%, new supply in Goa, Bengaluru and Delhi caps rates, TajSATS stays near 20% margins and hotel multiples stay at the bottom quartile after the sector de-rating.

parts.name: Hotels (owned, leased and managed)
parts.metricLabel: Sep-28E hotel EBITDA (½ FY28E + ½ FY29E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Post-Ind AS EBITDA; lease liabilities are in the net cash line. Multiple derived in the valuation chapter.

parts.name: TajSATS: IHCL's 51% at the same multiple
parts.note: Same EV/EBITDA as hotels (ICICI Securities values TajSATS on its hotel multiple) × 51%; SATS's 49% is therefore not deducted again.

parts.name: Less: minorities in hotel subsidiaries
parts.metricLabel: 5.0% (hotel minorities ÷ hotel profit before minorities) × hotel EV
parts.note: PIEM 41.35%, Benares 48.03%, St James Court 20.33%, United Hotels / NIHL ~45%, ANK, Pride, Atmantan and Brij 49% (AR FY26 note 39). Checked in INDHOTEL.ctx.js.

parts.name: Oriental Hotels (35.86%) at market less 20%, replacing book
parts.metricLabel: 6.40 cr shares × Rs142.36 (30-Sep-2026) × 0.8 − Rs322 cr book in model cash
parts.note: Listed associate; bull 10%, bear 30% discount. The 24-Aug-2026 merger scheme (25 IHCL for 117 OHL) is shown as a sensitivity.

parts.name: Less: Brij acquisition paid after Mar-26 (not in model cash)
parts.metricLabel: Up to Rs222 cr for 51% (IHCL ~Rs127 cr, ANK ~Rs34 cr, Pride ~Rs61 cr), completed 21-Apr-2026
parts.note: Brij's EBITDA is in our hotel forecasts from FY27; its 49% minority is in the hotel minorities line.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-28E (model: cash and investments less borrowings incl. leases)
parts.note: Mar-26: Screener cash Rs1,831 cr + investments Rs3,606 cr (incl. JVs/associates at book) − borrowings Rs2,837 cr (bank Rs51 cr + leases Rs2,786 cr) = Rs2,600 cr.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (EV/EBITDA)
methods.why: How the street values IHCL: EV/EBITDA on FY28E or Jun-28E EBITDA (ICICI Direct 29x, Axis 27x, Anand Rathi ~26x, Nomura ~23x), three as a SOTP that deducts minorities and adds Oriental Hotels and 51% of TajSATS (Motilal Oswal 28x, ICICI Securities 30x).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on attributable earnings: own forward P/E median adjusted for the sector P/E move.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, 12.2% discount rate, 6% terminal growth, plus net cash after leases.
